config.pageTitle: AQA GCSE Religious Studies A – Hinduism Revision
config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the published AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification (Hinduism, 3.1.4) and its five-part question structure (1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, from Summer 2026). They are not AQA past-paper questions. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other valid answers are credited in the exam.

Beliefs.1: 1-mark questions (AO1). Either a multiple-choice question (choose the correct letter from four options) or a 'Give one…' question. One accurate answer gains the mark; no development is needed. Spell key terms correctly.
Beliefs.4: 4-mark 'Explain two ways…' / 'Explain two contrasting…' questions (AO1). For each of two ways: simple explanation of a relevant and accurate point = 1 mark; detailed explanation (developed with an example, consequence or further information) = 2 marks. Two separate points, each developed, for full marks. For 'contrasting' questions the two points must differ (e.g. Advaita and Vaishnava views).
Beliefs.6: 6-mark 'Explain two… Refer to sacred writings or another source of Hindu belief and teaching in your answer' questions (AO1). Each of two teachings: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Source of authority: 2 marks for naming AND applying a relevant source (e.g. Bhagavad Gita 2.22, Rig Veda 10.129, an Upanishad, a guru or acharya), or 1 mark for naming it without applying it, or applying it without naming it.
Beliefs.12: 12-mark 'Evaluate this statement' questions (AO2) – refer to Hindu teaching, give reasoned arguments for the statement, give reasoned arguments for a different view, reach a justified conclusion. Level 4 (10–12): well-argued, reasoned consideration of different points of view; logical chains of reasoning leading to judgements supported by knowledge of relevant evidence; references to religion applied to the issue. Level 3 (7–9): reasoned consideration of different views; logical chains of reasoning; clear reference to religion. Level 2 (4–6): reasoned consideration of one view, or recognition of different views each supported by reasons – maximum Level 2 if there is no reference to religion. Level 1 (1–3): a point of view with reason(s). Up to 3 extra SPaG marks are awarded on the 12-mark questions in the Beliefs section.

Practices.1: 1-mark questions (AO1). Either a multiple-choice question (choose the correct letter from four options) or a 'Give one…' question. One accurate answer gains the mark; no development is needed.
Practices.4: 4-mark 'Explain two ways…' / 'Explain two contrasting…' questions (AO1). For each of two ways: simple explanation of a relevant and accurate point = 1 mark; detailed explanation = 2 marks. Use examples from Hindu practice in Britain or India today to develop points.
Practices.6: 6-mark 'Explain two… Refer to sacred writings or another source of Hindu belief and teaching in your answer' questions (AO1). Each of two points: simple = 1 mark, detailed = 2 marks. Source of authority: 2 marks for naming and applying a relevant source, 1 mark for naming only or applying only. Sources can include the Bhagavad Gita, Vedas, Upanishads, Ramayana, Puranas, the Yoga Sutras or a respected guru.
Practices.12: 12-mark 'Evaluate this statement' questions (AO2). Level 4 (10–12): well-argued, reasoned consideration of different points of view with logical chains of reasoning leading to a justified judgement and religion applied to the issue. Level 3 (7–9): reasoned consideration of different views, clear reference to religion. Level 2 (4–6): one view reasoned, or different views simply supported; maximum Level 2 without reference to religion. Level 1 (1–3): a view with reasons. (In the exam, SPaG marks for Hinduism are awarded on the Beliefs section 12-mark questions.)
